Describe a drawn sample

Source: R/plan.R
sample_summary.Rd

What you actually got, against what the design asked for. Worth a look before analysing: it surfaces strata that came up short, weights that vary more than you expected, and rows the design could never have reached.

Usage

sample_summary(sample)

Arguments

sample

A data frame returned by draw() with weights = TRUE.

Value

A list with a print() method, holding:

design

The design's type, as a string.

n, N

Rows drawn, and rows in the frame.

N_reachable

Rows of the frame the design gives a probability above 0, the population it samples. For weights conditional on the clusters selected, the rows of the clusters not selected count, since another selection could have drawn them. The printed sampling fraction is n / N_reachable. NA only when the frame's probabilities cannot be worked out, for an empty sample saved by drawn 0.2.0, which records none, from a design with no closed-form inclusion probability. The fraction is then n / N.

expected_n

The sample size the design expects, the sum of the inclusion probabilities over the frame. It is n for a design of fixed size, and printed beside n when the two differ, as they can under Poisson sampling, a design_systematic() interval that does not divide the frame, or clusters of unequal size. NA where N_reachable is, and for weights conditional on the clusters selected.

weight_range

The smallest and largest design weight.

weight_cv

Their coefficient of variation. Large values mean a few rows carry most of the estimate.

n_kish

Kish's effective sample size, sum(w)^2 / sum(w^2) over the weights w, which is n / (1 + cv^2) with the coefficient of variation computed with divisor n: the size of a simple random sample that would estimate a mean as precisely if unequal weights were the only cost. Clustering and stratification are not in it; deff() measures those.

n_certain

Sampled rows taken with certainty, at a probability of 1.

certain_by

Those rows by why they are certain, a named count: threshold, above the threshold of design_certainty(); size, put at probability 1 by a size measure, in design_weighted() or in design_spread() or design_multistage() with size, which includes the rows of a cluster put at 1 by its size and then taken whole; and whole, in a stratum, interval or cluster taken whole, or a census, with a size measure or without. Under a size measure a group counts as taken whole when the design gives every row of it probability 1, or every cluster of a multistage design a first-stage probability of 1, so a Poisson sample that holds every row of a stratum by chance files its certain rows under size.

conditional

The number of clusters selected, when the weights are conditional on them, as for design_cluster() with balanced = TRUE (see "Design weights" in draw()); otherwise NA.

unreachable

Frame rows with inclusion probability 0, which the design could never have selected, such as rows na_rm drops. NA where N_reachable is.

by_group

A data frame of group, drawn, in_frame and rate per stratum, interval or cluster, or NULL for a design with no grouping. The strata are those of design_stratified(), and of design_spread() and design_weighted() when they have strata, and every stratum of the frame is listed, one allocated no rows included. A stratum's in_frame counts the rows the design can draw from it, as N of allocation_table() does, so rows na_rm drops are left out, and a stratum it empties is not listed. The intervals of design_temporal() are listed in time order and named by their start, such as "2024-01-03 00:00". For design_cluster() and design_multistage(), only the clusters drawn are listed. For design_certainty(), the groups are those of its rest over the rows below the threshold, after a "(certain)" row for the rows above it.

group_col

The column(s) by_group is keyed on.

drawn

How the sample was drawn, from its drawn_meta attribute: seed, rng_kind, version, time, frame_rows and made_by (see "Seeding" in draw()). NULL for a sample from an earlier version of drawn, which recorded none. The print shows the seed, the version and the date.

See also

draw(), deff()

Examples

set.seed(1)
pop <- data.frame(
  id = 1:400,
  site = rep(c("a", "b", "c", "d"), times = c(200, 100, 60, 40))
)
s <- draw(pop, design_stratified("site", n = 40), seed = 1, weights = TRUE)
sample_summary(s)
#> Sample of 40 from 400  (stratified design)
#>   sampling fraction  0.1
#>   design weights     10 to 10   (cv 0)
#>   effective n        40  (Kish, from the weights alone)
#>   drawn              with seed 1, by drawn 0.2.0.9000 on 2026-11-18
#> 
#>   by site:
#>     group  drawn  in frame   rate
#>     a         20      200  0.100
#>     b         10      100  0.100
#>     c          6       60  0.100
#>     d          4       40  0.100
